inverness.snapshot: Inverness is a full-fibre city at the head of the Highlands, and its telecoms trade runs two ways. The build contractors and cabling firms putting crews across the city tend to run trade accounts and kit whole teams in branded workwear, while the ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. We run both routes side by side, fleet and single installer alike.
inverness.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Inverness and the Highlands
s1loc: Inverness has had a heavy full-fibre build for a city its size. CityFibre delivered a 24 million pound network through build partner GCU Utilities and has now passed primary build, taking fibre to the premises past 28,000 homes, Openreach has full fibre widely available too, and toob has joined the CityFibre network in the city alongside the operators on top. Engineers from the major fibre and mobile networks work the streets and cabinets across districts like Dalneigh, Kinmylies, Hilton, Culloden, Smithton, Raigmore and Inshes, with civils crews and delivery partners trenching and pulling fibre right across the city.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a steady commercial scene. Structured-cabling and CCTV installers wire offices, units and warehouses in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre across the Longman Industrial Estate, Inverness Campus, Beechwood Business Park, Stoneyfield and the Inverness Airport Business Park out toward Dalcross. The trade runs from contractors cabling whole office floors to one-van installers fitting a single shopfront camera, and all of them need hard-wearing branded workwear for work across the city's premises.
